 Laser speckle extensometer 
 Laser speckle extensometer
The laser speckle extensometer is a non-contact deformation measuring device for material testing, based on laser speckle evaluation.
 Schematic structure of the measuring system:
(1) High-resolution CCD cameras for detection
(2) Laser diodes for generating the speckle patterns
 Measuring principle
The test object is illuminated with laser light, which creates a "speckle pattern" on the surface of the sample. During the tensile test, the pattern is continuously recorded by two cameras. At the beginning of the measurement, the "speckle pattern" coming from the object is recorded by the cameras and stored as a reference. Each time the cameras take another image, the pattern of the reference image is searched for in the image and the offset or displacement is calculated.
Setup: 2 laser diodes - 2 speckle patterns - 2 detector cameras
 Laser speckle extensometer
Advantages 
no sample marking necessary, but generation of the speckle pattern by the laser 
use in temperature chamber possible 
tests on a variety of materials possible
